The unifying ideas across all SAE work.
Each column of W_dec is a
A wider-than-input autoencoder trained to be SPARSE (few active latents per input).
Hypothesis: LLM activations are compositional and decompose into interpretable directions.
SAE architecture: forward pass + two losses
L1 encourages z_i = 0 for most i.
Result: only a few latents 'fire' per token.
This is what makes an SAE 'sparse'.
Trained by SGD on activations x sampled
• Each colored ARROW is one decoder column
• Given input x, encoder computes z[i] =
the STRENGTH of feature i in x.
• d_sae >> d_model, so we have many MORE
directions than a basis. Sparsity picks
Neurons in an LLM don't correspond to interpretable concepts one-for-one.
Instead, ONE neuron activates for many unrelated things, and ONE concept is
Why: d_model is small (say 768) but the model represents many more than
768 features. So features get SUPERPOSED into d_model via non-orthogonal
directions. SAEs undo the superposition by making d_sae much wider.
L1 penalty sum(|z_i|) induces SPARSITY: many z_i are exactly 0.
Intuition: L2 encourages small values everywhere; L1 encourages
MOST values to be 0 while a few can be large.
Geometrically: the L1 ball has corners at the axes, so the loss's
minimum tends to land at 'axis points' where most coordinates
SAE variants: transcoders, meta-SAE, TopK, gated, JumpReLU
Standard SAE = ReLU + L1. Many variants tweak either the ACTIVATION or the LOSS.
Some target different things entirely (transcoders replace MLPs; meta-SAE re-analyses SAEs).
+ fixed k active features per token
+ no L1 penalty → no activation shrinkage
- k is a hyperparameter to tune
Transcoders: like SAEs, but replace MLPs (Marks et al. 2024)
Goal: L(x_hat, x) small; z sparse.
→ latents = decompositions of the residual stream.
Transcoder (predicts MLP OUTPUT from MLP INPUT)
Goal: L(y_hat, MLP(x)) small; z sparse.
→ latents = interpretable APPROXIMATION of an MLP.
You can REPLACE the MLP with a sparse sum of latents.
a SPARSE way to describe what
each MLP is DOING to residual
in a forward pass and re-inspect
Meta-SAE and Attention SAE (SAEs on top of SAEs / on attention)
Idea: train ANOTHER SAE, but on the LATENTS of the first SAE.
The second SAE learns 'meta-features': re-usable clusters of the
primary features that light up together.
Result: dendrogram over primary features → interpretable groups.
e.g. meta-feature = 'Python code', primary features it covers:
→ another axis on which SAEs decompose the representation.
Idea: separate SAE per HEAD (or per LAYER) trained on that head's
attention output. Recovers head-specific interpretable features.
• Attention heads often carry a MIX of behaviours.
An attention SAE tells you 'this head fires feature 42 (=
duplicate-token detector) when this input pattern happens'.
• Useful for CIRCUIT ANALYSIS: attribute what a specific head
contributes to a downstream feature, in feature-space.
Cheat sheet: when to use which variant
k must be tuned per layer
Feature splitting: as SAE gets wider, features refactor into sub-features
Splitting tree: root feature (narrow) → children (wider) → grandchildren (widest)
UMAP of SAE decoder directions W_dec: same clusters, more resolution
one broad point per cluster (heavy overlap)
Each dot = one decoder column W_dec[i], projected to 2D via UMAP over cosine similarity of decoder directions.
As d_sae grows, one dot from the narrow SAE turns into a small CLUSTER of nearby dots in the wide SAE.
→ features refactor: 'code' at d_sae=512 becomes {Python, JS, shell, Markdown} at 4K, which further split at 32K.
L0 grows ~ log(d_sae), not linearly with width.
→ more features doesn't mean more fire per token.
In narrow SAE, one latent must cover both
It fires on either → confusion, less specific.
Widen the SAE: NEW capacity means the
one broad feature can specialise into
on exactly one of the two contexts.
Math: overcomplete dictionary D of atoms d_i,
x ≈ sum_i c_i d_i, c sparse (L1).
This is why we say 'feature', not 'neuron':
features SPLIT and MERGE as capacity changes.
Wider SAEs also produce DEAD FEATURES: latents that never fire on any input.
As d_sae grows, the fraction of alive features drops. Anthropic reports ~20% dead at 32x expansion.
Mitigations: ghost gradients, resample dead neurons, decayed L1, or use TopK / Gated SAE architectures (see §6).
